correctness.rationale: Fix A and U=im A. For uniform B the map B|_U is uniform in Hom(U,V), and postcomposing with the surjection A produces a uniform endomorphism of U. Since AB lands in U, nilpotency is equivalent to nilpotency of its restriction (at most one extra iterate is needed). The Fine–Herstein count then gives conditional probability q^(−rank A), including rank zero. This equals Pr(Aw=0|A) for an independent uniform vector w. Apply it to the product T of the first k−1 factors (T=I for k=1). The probability that Tw is nonzero is (1−q^(−n))^k: w must start nonzero, and each independent uniform factor encountered from right to left maps a given nonzero vector to a uniform vector. A nilpotent radical preserves and reflects nilpotency on passage to the quotient, since x^m in J and J^s=0 imply x^(ms)=0. Equal fibers give independent uniform quotient inputs; the direct-product block probabilities multiply. The zero ring has probability one. Frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed. Its 21 comparisons are exact finite convolutions for the selected matrix rings over prime fields and three additional rings, not verification of the all-rings or all-length quantifiers.
